# Verity One

Verity One is a local-first memory layer and knowledge graph for AI agents: your local node runs on your own machine and is the source of truth.

## Human pages

- /: Home — what Verity One is and why the local node is the source of truth.
- /start: Start — the shortest path: install, connect an agent, first recall.
- /agents: Agents — how agents connect, the authority model, and what they must not assume.
- /trust: Trust — what stays local, what the hosted mirror does, and the honest limits.
- /plus: VO+ — the optional web bridge that carries memory beyond the desk on demand.
- /docs: Docs — reference for installing, connecting, and operating a local node.
- /download: Download — source-only install (one-line script builds from the pinned commit).

## Live machine entry points

- GET /: discovery — content-negotiated JSON describing the system and its routes.
- /schema: the ontology — node types, edge types, property and confidence semantics.
- /.well-known/agent: agent descriptor — protocol, version, capabilities, bootstrap steps.
- /connect: onboarding packet — system prompt and the routes a new agent needs to start.
- /toc: full node listing for the visible public knowledge graph.
- /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server: OAuth metadata — endpoints, S256 PKCE, scopes.
- /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource: the protected resource (verityone.app/mcp) and its scopes.

## Authority

Authority is the local stdio MCP server vo-mcp, which has full read and write access to the local node. The local node does NOT serve a web MCP endpoint — web MCP lives only at verityone.app/mcp. Hosted reads are a mirror of the last sync, not live authority. The hosted mirror is not zero-knowledge.
